verdict_rationale: 0 high/medium findings. 1 low finding (pre-existing mgba test gap, out of TSK-123 scope). TSK-123 is a documentation-and-testing task that fully delivers: mgba BTN map verification by inspection + comment, wasmboy no-op documented at both BTN map and sendInput guard, 5 new tests across stub-engine and wasmboy-engine covering all required invariants (no-throw, no setJoypadState call, regression isolation). Code quality is high throughout the diff.
summary: TSK-123 delivers targeted documentation and test coverage for the L/R shoulder-button pipeline across three engine adapters. For mgba-engine, the BTN map already contained l/r entries from TSK-060; TSK-123 adds an explanatory block comment and cross-reference. For wasmboy-engine, the no-op semantics (guard `if (!key) return`) are now explicitly documented in both the BTN map header and sendInput guard, aligning with US-062 BR §4. Two new describe blocks (stub-engine.test.ts: 2 tests; wasmboy-engine.test.ts: 3 tests) provide direct evidence of the invariants: StubEngine accepts l/r without exception, WasmBoyEngine does not forward l/r to setJoypadState, and mapped buttons (a, b, …) continue to work correctly after a no-op l/r sequence. One pre-existing issue is noted: mgba-engine.ts has no test file; sendInput contains non-trivial branching but in-repo WASM testing is acknowledged as infeasible in the file header. This gap is outside TSK-123's scope and does not affect correctness of this delivery.
